items.definition:
to close (one's hand or teeth) tightly, typically in anger or determination
He had to clench his fists to stop himself from shouting.

to make a series of short, sharp noises
The fire began to crackle merrily in the fireplace.

convert (information or an image) into digital form
We need to digitize all our old paper records.

cut up (a body or plant) to study its internal parts; analyze in detail
The students had to dissect a frog in biology class.

make something seem less important than it really is
The politician tried to downplay the severity of the economic crisis.

evade or escape from (a danger, enemy, or pursuer), typically in a skillful or cunning way
The suspect managed to elude the police for several days.

destroy completely
The company was hired to exterminate the pests in the building.

disturb or disconcert (someone)
Nothing seemed to faze the experienced pilot during the turbulence.

to give incorrect information to
The news report might misinform the public.

to fall or drop straight down at high speed
The stock market began to plummet after the announcement.

to expand and contract with strong regular movements
He could feel his heart pulsate rapidly after the run.

to lean or lie back in a relaxed position
She liked to recline on the sofa and read a book.

launch again
The company decided to relaunch the product with new features.

disarrange (especially hair or feathers); annoy
The wind began to ruffle her hair.

to estimate below the true worth
Don't undervalue your skills; they are very important.

To officially declare (information or documents) to be no longer secret.
The government decided to declassify the old intelligence reports.

To separate or release (someone or something) from something to which they are attached or involved.
He tried to disengage himself from the argument.

To make (someone) lose their sense of direction or feel confused.
The sudden loud noise seemed to disorient the birds.

lift or haul (a heavy thing) with great effort
They had to heave the heavy box onto the truck.

To wander aimlessly; to follow a winding course.
The river meanders through the valley.

to provide with food or other substances necessary for growth, health, and good condition
Good food will nourish your body and mind.

to evaluate again or differently
We need to reevaluate our strategy after these new developments.

show again, play again
They decided to rerun the old TV series.

to allow air to enter and circulate freely
It's important to ventilate the room regularly.

to make or become white
She used a special product to whiten her teeth.

to identify and remove errors from computer hardware or software
It took hours to debug the code and find the source of the error.

to cease to use
The company disused the old factory after moving to a new site.

to make something smaller; to reduce the number of employees
The company decided to downsize its workforce to cut costs.

To slowly trickle or seep out of something.
Mud began to ooze from the cracks in the wall.

To satisfy (thirst) or extinguish (fire).
He drank a large glass of water to quench his thirst.

To justify with logical reasons, often false ones.
He tried to rationalize his decision, but it was clearly a mistake.

to waste something in a reckless and foolish manner
Don't squander your opportunities; make the most of them.

to make something free from bacteria or other living microorganisms
It's important to sterilize medical instruments before use.

to be suitable for; to suit
Such behavior does not befit a leader.

to be full to the point of overflowing
The cup was brimming with hot coffee.

to make a situation less tense or dangerous
The diplomat tried to defuse the tense situation.

To castrate or spay (an animal).
We decided to neuter our cat to prevent unwanted litters.

To combine or cause to combine with oxygen.
Iron will oxidize and rust if exposed to air and moisture.

To cause (a person or part of the body) to become immobile.
The accident left him paralysed from the waist down.

To make or become dry through intense heat.
The sun began to parch the land, turning the grass brown.

introduce again
They plan to reintroduce wolves into the national park.

supply again
The troops needed to resupply their ammunition.

come or bring to the surface again
The submarine will resurface in an hour.

increase very rapidly and suddenly
The company's profits skyrocketed last quarter.

faint from extreme emotion; be overcome with admiration
She would swoon every time she saw her favorite pop star.

to decay or break down
Organic matter will decompose over time.

to dislike intensely
I absolutely detest cold weather.

to wave or swing wildly
He began to flail his arms to get attention.

to shine with a sparkling light
The dew drops glistened on the grass in the morning sun.

to move toward or be attracted to a place, person, or thing
People tend to gravitate towards those with similar interests.

to confuse or mix up
Don't muddle the papers on my desk.

exist or occur at an earlier date than
Dinosaurs predated humans by millions of years.

shape again or differently
The new policy will reshape the future of the industry.

imbue with new life and vitality
The city plans to revitalize the downtown area with new businesses.

to join or connect
They had to splice the two pieces of film together.

to deliberately destroy or damage property
Someone tried to vandalize the public park last night.

to breathe with a whistling sound
He started to wheeze after running up the stairs.

to make someone or something seem unimportant
Don't belittle her efforts; she worked very hard.

to give the different forms of a verb
In Spanish class, we learned how to conjugate regular verbs.

cause someone to lose determination or confidence
Don't let one failure dishearten you as you pursue your goals.

secretly listen to a private conversation
It's rude to eavesdrop on other people's conversations.

complete (a process or arrangement); bring to an end
We need to finalise the details of the contract by tomorrow.

to write something quickly
I'll just jot down a few notes.

Make or become quicker.
The pace of the music began to quicken.
